analysis.logline: At his own promotion party, a husband publicly throws out the wife who has quietly carried him, and her calm last instruction tells the room that his pride rests on something she controls.
analysis.tone: Family-friendly but cutting domestic drama: loud party cruelty on one side, held-back dignity on the other, ending on a half-laugh that has lost its confidence.

events.text: establishing view of INT. KALIO DUPLEX, PETER ODILI ROAD, PORT HARCOURT. NIGHT
Rain hammers the windows.
A promotion party is in full swing: twenty guests, a generator humming behind the wall, glasses clinking.
RICHARD KALIO (38), tight burgundy shirt, gold-rimmed sunglasses pushed up into his fade, holds a glass high and turns a heavy gold watch on his wrist.
At his elbow stands STEPHANIE SEKIBO (29), fuchsia dress, glossy bob, long French-tip nails.
ESTHER KALIO (33), in a plain sage-green wrapper and blouse, crosses the room with a tray of fried plantain and small chops, her head down.

events.speaker: RICHARD
events.text: Look at her! A primary school teacher, carrying plantain in my sitting room like a house girl. Esther, who asked you to serve my guests?

events.speaker: ESTHER
events.text: You did, Richard. This morning.

events.speaker: RICHARD
events.text: I asked you to stay in the kitchen. Not to stand where my colleagues can see you.

events.speaker: STEPHANIE
events.text: Richard, leave her. She is trying. Not everybody can be at this level.
